speaker: Editorial year heading
title: 1983--1984 year heading and overlapping catalogue provenance
summary: This is an annual heading, not a mathematical lecture, and has zero items. P001113--P001114 contain adjacent April 1983 material belonging to the prior volume: moment-map/Duistermaat--Heckman material should be linked to1982-596.1--3, and zeta-function continuation to1982-595.1--7. The broad catalogue span overlaps later autumn lectures; actual source headings control their boundaries. This record is kept to preserve the supplied inventory.

speaker: P. Deligne
title: Monodromy, families of abelian varieties, and hypergeometric lattices
summary: The explicit5 September Deligne heading is on P001115; the talk continues into the upper portion of P001116 and ends before the 12 September Arnold heading. The catalogue's broader P001113--P001115 range contains prior-April material and must not determine mathematical attribution. The notes mix local monodromy, semistable abelian degenerations, a degree bound, Deligne--Mostow examples and rational monodromy finiteness. The fixed-base hypotheses and equivalence relation are essential.

speaker: V. I. Arnold, with seminar comments
title: Sperner theory, polytopes, reflection groups, and quadratic dynamics
summary: The12 September heading in the lower part of P001116 follows Deligne. Arnold discusses rectangular partition posets and hard Lefschetz, the polytope g-theorem, Vinberg's dimension bound and the quadratic map \(z^2+i\). Bare notices of Sato, MacPherson and Yau do not identify new mathematical problems. The parameter-density remark lacks an ambient set and must not be silently converted into the density-of-hyperbolicity conjecture.

speaker: A. M. Perelomov
title: Chiral models, topology of solitons, and Witten's topological term
summary: The lecture begins on P001120 and ends before Daletskii's3 October heading on P001123. It moves from symmetry and particle interactions to sigma models, coadjoint-orbit instantons, scaling and the Skyrme term, and the five-dimensional Wess--Zumino functional. Several shorthand assertions require missing compactness, simple-connectedness, first-order self-duality and period-normalization hypotheses. P001122 was inspected for the decisive homotopy and scaling formulas.

speaker: Yu. L. Daletskii
title: Lie--Poisson brackets, kinetic equations, and point-particle reductions
summary: Daletskii's heading begins in the lower part of P001123 and continues on P001124 until the explicit Beilinson heading. The date line reads3/X-84 in the transcription and scan context, but the surrounding autumn1983 sequence supports3 October1983 as the editorial session date; the discrepancy is retained. The lecture realizes particle and Vlasov equations in a dual Poisson algebra and mentions a graded extension with Kadobianskii, whose exact publication remains unidentified.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Witten's SU(2) anomaly and the topological obstruction
summary: Although the catalogue supplies no page links, the lower part of P001124 explicitly labels Beilinson and leads into the anomaly discussion on P001125. These surviving notes are assigned to603 by source-heading evidence, with reconstructed attribution and the 3/X-84 versus1983 date discrepancy retained. The argument concerns an odd number of Weyl doublets, a Pfaffian sign, suspension topology and a real mod2 index; it does not define a rigorous interacting gauge-field path integral.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson, with I. M. Gelfand's question
title: Dirac families, mapping tori, and the anomaly sign
summary: The17 October Beilinson continuation uses a chiral Dirac family and a mapping torus to interpret spectral flow. The Pauli commutator normalization, real skew-adjoint structure and endpoint identification must be fixed. Gelfand asks for a mathematical framework; determinant/Pfaffian lines and later eta-invariant holonomy provide a precise partial realization, while the broad construction of an interacting quantum field theory is not claimed solved.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Symmetric functions, standard bases, and tableaux
summary: The lecture introduces the graded ring of symmetric functions, its elementary, complete, power-sum and Schur bases, and the Kostka-tableau rule. The first two lines of P001130 finish this lecture before the 24 October heading. Strict positivity of every Kostka number and unrestricted integral generation by power sums require correction.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Formal wave functions, Cherednik's identity, and tau-functions
summary: The24 October heading on P001130 begins a formal differential-operator calculation continuing through equation 17 on P001131. The logarithmic derivative, fractional powers and tau quotient have identifiable classical sources. The Lax sign, quotient derivative, two different potentials called tau, and omitted spectral powers require explicit normalization. The theorem number 3.1 does not match the located 1978 Cherednik paper, where the identity is Theorem 1.4.

speaker: G. I. Olshanskii
title: Representations of the stable unitary group from oscillator and spin models
summary: The named Olshanskii heading follows the tau-function discussion on P001131. Conjugated embeddings into stable symplectic groups produce representation families, whose infinitesimal oscillator formulas continue on P001132. The unqualified full-Fock irreducibility assertion omits the component selection required in the published dual-pair construction.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Symmetric-function transition matrices
summary: The lecture repeats the graded ring and standard bases, then interprets transition coefficients by nonnegative, zero-one and weighted-assignment matrices. On P001134 the explicit I.M.G. partition-number aside interrupts the exposition; the Schur alternant formula below it resumes the symmetric-function discussion. These repeated occurrences remain indexed separately.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand; an unattributed continuation
title: Partition numbers and an unattributed anomaly recap
summary: The explicit \ru{И.М.Г.} passage on P001134 concerns partition asymptotics and Euler's product. The Witten-anomaly recap at the beginning of P001135 has no speaker label and precedes the named Perelomov heading. It is included as an unattributed continuation of the same session, with no claim that Gelfand authored it. The multi-term partition formula is not written, so its exact version cannot be uniquely identified.

speaker: A. M. Perelomov
title: Chiral fields, Skyrme terms, and multivalued actions
summary: The named Perelomov section begins below the anomaly recap on P001135 and ends on P001136; the 14 November material starts on P001137. It revisits two-dimensional instantons and the Skyrme correction, mentions Krichever's nonlinear d'Alembert construction, and compares Witten's topological term with Novikov's multivalued variational framework.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: The one-dimensional Ising model
summary: Periodic spins, action normalizations and local statistical weights. First physical heading on this date.

speaker: V. A. Chulaevskii
title: Gibbs measures and correlations
summary: Marginal speaker heading attached to the correlation discussion following Gelfand.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Partitions and Dyson ranks
summary: Ramanujan congruences, rank equidistribution and direct bijection questions.

speaker: A. M. Vershik
title: Asymptotic representation theory and the K-functor
summary: Joint work with S. V. Kerov: dimensions, random diagrams, characters and the ordered Grothendieck ring.

speaker: A. A. Migdal; opening remark by I. M. Gelfand
title: Large-dimensional integrals and loop equations
summary: Spherical and matrix examples, entropy, factorization, resolvents and loop equations; ends before the Wiegmann heading.

speaker: P. B. Wiegmann
title: Principal chiral fields and determinants
summary: Exact-solution announcement, fermionic determinants and multivalued chiral actions.

speaker: P. B. Wiegmann
title: Fermionization and the Bethe ansatz
summary: Current interactions, auxiliary fields, determinant identities and the spinful contact gas.

speaker: V. Ginzburg; P. B. Wiegmann
title: Compactification; continued integrable models
summary: V. Ginzburg opens on P001154; the explicit P. Wiegmann continuation on that page owns the remainder. The catalogue expansion V. L. is unconfirmed.

title: YEAR 1984
summary: Catalogue year heading, with no separate mathematical occurrence in the supplied source.

speaker: I. V. Cherednik
title: Quadratic exchange algebras and finite-dimensional elliptic representations
summary: The report itself begins on P001164 and ends on P001166. P001162–P001163 belong to the preceding Wiegmann material, and P001167 begins Zelevinsky’s report. The central new result has a close match in Cherednik’s two-page paper received 23 February 1984, three days after the seminar; the elliptic \(R\)-matrix and rank-two Sklyanin algebra have earlier sources.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky, joint work with I. M. Gelfand
title: Models of classical-group representations and hidden symmetries
summary: The actual report begins on P001167 and ends in the upper part of P001170; Nikiforov begins below it on that page. Its model tables, basic Grassmannians, and hidden actions match Gelfand–Zelevinsky’s 1984 paper, received 15 March 1984. The paper explicitly separates proved even constructions from a supergroup formulation whose proof is deferred. Gelfand’s brief research suggestions are recorded separately without invented conjectures.

speaker: A. F. Nikiforov
title: Hypergeometric equations, discrete orthogonal polynomials, and angular momentum
summary: Nikiforov’s heading begins in the lower part of P001170 and the report ends on P001171. The catalogue’s “F. Nikiforov” is identified as A. F. Nikiforov. The material matches Nikiforov–Suslov–Uvarov’s 1985 paper and 1991 English monograph; their cited preprints from 1982 and 1983 show that the main discrete-polynomial correspondences already predated this seminar.

speaker: Yu. M. Berezanskii
title: The half-line Toda chain by inverse spectral reconstruction
summary: The report begins on P001172 and ends in the upper part of P001173; Fradkin begins below it. Its bounded half-line inverse-spectral theorem closely matches Berezanskii’s 1985 note, received 9 April 1984. That note says the approach had already been presented in Kyiv in October 1983, so the seminar is not asserted to be the first public announcement.

speaker: E. S. Fradkin
title: Gauge unification and supergravity
summary: The actual report begins in the lower part of P001173, after Berezanskii, and continues through P001174. Catalogue overlap does not assign the Toda discussion to Fradkin. The report combines standard gauge constructions, a tentative \(E_8\) unification programme, bibliographic pointers, and Gelfand’s question about an infinite-dimensional geometric space.

speaker: E. S. Fradkin
title: Gauge mass generation, extended supergravity, and open gauge algebras
summary: The dated report occupies P001175–P001176. It revisits gauge curvature, renormalization, spontaneous symmetry breaking, extended supermultiplets, conformal gravity, functional integration, and quantization of gauge algebras that close modulo equations of motion. These are separate assertions with different degrees of precision.

speaker: D. A. Leites
title: Lie superalgebras and exceptional families
summary: The heading on P001177 begins Leites’s report; it continues through P001178, before Penkov’s heading on P001179. It introduces superspaces, signs, matrix families, invariant forms, traces, and two exceptional constructions. A short question about Jordan form remains underspecified. The remaining matrix formulas were read in the supplied transcription; the outage prevented a final visual recheck of P001178.

speaker: I. B. Penkov
title: Typical Borel–Weil–Bott theory for special linear supergroups
summary: Penkov’s heading is on P001179, after Leites. The report concerns \(SL(n|m)\), parity-dependent full flags, line bundles, and the typical-weight analogue of Borel–Weil–Bott. The exact result is documented in Penkov’s later full treatment; the short 1984 announcement is distinguished from the 1988/1990 exposition.

speaker: I. B. Penkov
title: Superflags, homogeneous line bundles, and affine flag constructions
summary: The continuation occupies P001180–P001181. It repeats the typical theorem and character construction, mentions a differential-operator version, and illustrates flags and additional volume data. Here “affine flags” means flags with determinant data or the homogeneous space \(G/N\), not the affine flag variety of a loop group.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: Verma modules and singular vectors for affine sl2
summary: Fuchs’s dated report begins on P001182 and ends in the upper part of P001183, before Beilinson’s heading. It defines the derived affine algebra, Verma modules and reducibility, asks about Casimirs, and introduces the formal-power method later published by Malikov, Feigin, and Fuchs. The notes mix a lowest-weight definition with a highest-weight reducibility formula; both conventions are separated below.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Mixed Hodge structures and absolute Hodge cohomology
summary: Beilinson’s heading is in the lower part of P001183, after Fuchs, and the report continues through P001185. It introduces pure and mixed real Hodge structures, canonical complex splittings, an operator comparing conjugate splittings, Tate objects, and Ext groups, ending with a derived-cohomology programme. The category and coefficient ring must be kept explicit; the checked Ext formula below is for real mixed Hodge structures.

speaker: Ya. G. Sinai
title: Critical Ising fields and renormalization; a perverse-sheaf aside
summary: Separates the finite-volume model, phase regimes, critical block limits, and universality. A final MacPherson allusion supplies no reconstructible theorem.

speaker: Jean-Pierre Serre
title: Centres, fixed points, and property (FA)
summary: The Serre material occurs above the Margulis note on P001187, despite catalogue numbering.

speaker: G. A. Margulis
title: Higher-rank lattices and actions on trees
summary: A short generalization follows Serre's examples in the physical notebook order.

title: Academic-year heading 1984--85
summary: Documentary heading only; it is not a mathematical talk.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Lipschitz structures, signature operators, and slice areas; Grothendieck programme
summary: Separates the earlier Lipschitz index theorem from later local characteristic formulas, checks two operator displays, and gives a precise form of the slice-area question.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Catalan numbers, special linear systems, and finite SU(2) groups
summary: The enumerative count requires a general curve; the finite-group discussion requires binary lifts and distinguishes the quotient surface, Milnor fibre, and Cartan form. An unattributed groupoid note follows.

speaker: M. A. Semenov-Tian-Shansky
title: Algebraic complete integrability, Laurent series, and Poisson--Lie geometry
summary: The local pole-count criterion is separated from compact abelian completion; the SO(4) formula remains partly unreadable. The later portion anticipates the 1985 dressing-action paper.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Atiyah--Singer: families of Dirac operators and anomalies
summary: The contractible connection space models a based gauge-group classifying space; the family index is a map into K-theory, and the anomaly involves a complex chiral determinant.

speaker: M. A. Semenov-Tian-Shansky
title: Poisson--Lie groups, doubles, dressing actions, and reduction
summary: Definitions and older r-matrix constructions lead to the speaker's 1985 action, leaf and reduction results. Repeated labels, a missing star, and an unjustified converse are retained as notebook errors and explicitly repaired.
